record.paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
record.original_question: For fixed integers k >= 3 and t, let P_t be the path on t vertices, and say that a graph is P_t-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to P_t. In k-Precoloring Extension, the input is a graph G together with a partial k-coloring of some vertices, and the question is whether that partial coloring can be extended to a proper k-coloring of all of G. In List k-Coloring, every vertex v has a list L(v) contained in {1, ..., k}, and the question is whether G has a proper coloring assigning each vertex a color from its list. For bipartite P_t-free graphs, what is the computational complexity of the unresolved cases: k-Precoloring Extension for t = 7, 8, or 9 with k = 3, 4, 5, or any fixed k >= 6, and for t >= 10 with k = 3; and List k-Coloring for t = 7 with k = 3, 4, 5, or any fixed k >= 6, and for t = 8, t = 9, or t >= 10 with k = 3?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let k ≥ 3 and t ≥ 1 be fixed integers. Let P_t denote the path on t vertices. A graph G is P_t-free if it contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to P_t. A graph is bipartite if its vertex set admits a partition into two independent sets. A proper k-coloring of G is a function c : V(G) → {1,…,k} with c(u) ≠ c(v) whenever uv ∈ E(G).

Consider the following decision problems restricted to bipartite P_t-free graphs:

(A) k-Precoloring Extension. Input: a bipartite P_t-free graph G and a partial map c₀ : W → {1,…,k} defined on some subset W ⊆ V(G) such that c₀ is a proper coloring of G[W]. Question: can c₀ be extended to a proper k-coloring of G?

(B) List k-Coloring. Input: a bipartite P_t-free graph G together with a list assignment L : V(G) → 2^{{1,…,k}}. Question: does there exist a proper coloring c of G with c(v) ∈ L(v) for every v ∈ V(G)?

Determine the computational complexity (polynomial-time solvable vs. NP-complete) of:

  • k-Precoloring Extension on bipartite P_t-free graphs for each of the cases t ∈ {7, 8, 9} with k ∈ {3, 4, 5} or any fixed k ≥ 6, and for t ≥ 10 with k = 3.

  • List k-Coloring on bipartite P_t-free graphs for t = 7 with k ∈ {3, 4, 5} or any fixed k ≥ 6, and for each of t = 8, t = 9, and t ≥ 10 with k = 3.
artifact.category_tag: Graph coloring complexity on H-free graphs
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search shows continued progress on List k-Coloring and Precoloring Extension restricted to P_t-free bipartite graphs (e.g., NP-completeness of 4-PreExt on P_10-free chordal bipartite graphs, 4-List Coloring on P_8-free chordal bipartite graphs, polynomial-time algorithms for comb-/caterpillar-convex bipartite subclasses in 2023–2024). However, no source resolves the full set of listed open cases on general bipartite P_t-free graphs; the entries remain marked as unresolved in subsequent surveys.

status_evidence.title: Coloring Problems on Bipartite Graphs of Small Diameter
status_evidence.snippet: Precoloring Extension is NP-complete on P_13-free bipartite graphs; 4-PreExt is NP-complete on P_10-free chordal bipartite graphs; 4-List Coloring is NP-complete on P_8-free chordal bipartite graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Hardness results push lower bounds but do not close the listed gaps for general bipartite P_t-free graphs.

status_evidence.title: List 3-Coloring on Comb-Convex and Caterpillar-Convex Bipartite Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial-time algorithm for List 3-Coloring on caterpillar-convex bipartite graphs, a restricted subclass.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress on restricted subclasses, not resolving the bipartite P_t-free cases.
